Institute for Industrial Productivity (IIP) (c. 2013). Industrial Efficiency Technology Database (IETD): Ammonia, Cement, Iron and Steel, Pulp and Paper, Glass and Motor Systems technology pages. Online database, formerly at http://ietd.iipnetwork.org/ and www.iipinetwork.org/wp-content/Ietd/; offline since; archived content retrieved from the Internet Archive Wayback Machine, capture of 15 November 2019 (timestamp 20191115221859), crawled 2026-10-07. No DOI.

2013: the newest works cited on the pages are 2013 (FAI 2013; ArcelorMittal 2013), the FAI ammonia overview runs to 2011-12, and the sector Key Data cite World Steel Association 2012; UKERC cites the same database as 'IIP 2012'/'ITP 2012' (accessed 11 September 2012) and 'IETD 2013'. The footer carries no year.

ietd_2013_industrial-efficiency-technology-database_iip-wayback-crawl.json (coordinator's Chrome crawl, 367 pages: {source, sectors, pages{file:{title,sectors,url,text}}}); ietd_2013_industrial-efficiency-technology-database_iip-iron-and-steel.mhtml (user's saved iron-and-steel sector page, Benchmarks/Key Data tabs).

Locator convention: no page numbers exist; 'reference' gives the IETD page file name (as in the crawl JSON keys, URL .../wp-content/Ietd/content/<file>), the table row (technology name as printed) or the Costs & Benefits column. In-text citations printed on the pages (e.g. 'US EPA, 2010. p.20', 'NEDO, 2008. p.74', 'Worrell et al., 2010', 'FAI, 2013') are carried as 'reprinted from <work> (page)'; values with no printed citation have no reprint note. Pages: 367 crawled = 185 stubs with no content (Wayback 'has not archived that URL', JavaScript-only or 404 pages: all 50 glass pages, 38 of 47 motor-systems pages, 76 cement, 18 ammonia, 3 iron and steel/pulp), 70 organisation/program/support-programme pages (skipped), 1 cross-sector motor-systems overview (sector statistics and chart data only, skipped), 1 pulp technology page with publications only (black-liquor-solids-concentration), and 111 pages used: 29 process pages (each a table: technology, Energy Savings Potential, CO2 Emission Reduction Potential, Costs, Development Status), 80 technology 'Costs & Benefits' pages (their text duplicates the process-page rows except for the four cement technology pages and two recovered-fibre pages whose process pages were not archived), and the FAI overview of Indian ammonia plants. Main file: whole-technology SEC, capex/opex, emissions and status (124 examples, 64 technology names); incremental retrofit capex of measures that map to *_efficiency-* archetypes (COST BASIS: incremental); plant-specific cases are separate examples ('- <case>' suffix in process). _measures: savings versus existing practice with their costs and paybacks, one row per technology entry or case (329 rows). _flows: recovered steam/electricity, coal, oxygen and electrode rates (18). _other-values: the Worrell et al. 2008 world best practice benchmark table from the sector page, primary energy, sector statistics, FAI projections (34). Price years: most costs print no year; per spec they carry 2013_ with 'PRICE YEAR NOT STATED'. Many are reprints of US EPA 2010 (which states 2008 dollars), Worrell et al. 2010, NEDO 2008 (yen), IPPC BREFs, CSI/ECRA 2009, Martin et al. 2000, Kramer et al. 2009 and US DOE 2003; years printed on the page ('2005 values', '2002 dollars', '1998') are used. 'tpd' and 'tonne' are taken as metric tonnes. No heating-value basis is stated anywhere. Overlap: much of the iron and steel content reprints US EPA 2010 and Worrell et al. 2010 (worrell_2010_001, already extracted) and APP SOACT 2010; the pulp content reprints Kramer et al. 2009 and Martin et al. 2000; ammonia costs reprint FAI 2013 and ECCJ 1999. Expect duplicates against those extractions when pooling.

(1) CDQ page prints '1 JPY = US $0.1257' (factor 10 too high). (2) Consteel: '$3.2 million 500,000 t/y, or $7.8/t' but 3.2e6/500,000 = 6.4. (3) Grate cooler cost low end printed '$.044' (0.44 likely). (4) SL/RN 'Total CO emissions are 3.2 t/t' (CO2 likely). (5) Limestone cement CO2 '50 to 140 t CO2/t-cement' (kg intended). (6) Mineralizers '0.05 to 018 GJ/t'. (7) Brownstock washing '001 GJ/ton'. (8) TRT citation 'NEDO, 200'; hot stove 'EIA, 2007' (IEA). (9) Davenport cement motors '2.1 MWh' (2.1 million kWh). (10) GBFS cement row title printed in Chinese. (11) 'Heat Recovery from Cooling Water' saving printed '0.0 GJ/t'. (12) Residue injection 'BF with 2.5 t-HM/day capacity'. (13) Waste heat EAF electricity '2.8 MWh/y' and '15.1 MWh/y' implausibly small. All kept as printed in notes; none corrected.
